correctness.rationale: The source proves \(\Pr(T>t)\sim C t^{-1/\beta}\) with \(C>0\). The nonnegative-tail identity for real moments then gives convergence iff \(r<1/\beta\), and at equality the tail integral is asymptotic to a positive constant times \(\int dt/t\). Thus at \(\beta=1/2\) the second moment and variance diverge, while the mean remains finite. The consequences for CV, standardized skewness, and kurtosis follow from their defining moment requirements.
